requirements.statement: The arrival date is one text input enhanced by the MoJ date picker: a 'Choose date' button opens a calendar dialog with Previous year, Previous month, Next month and Next year buttons, a month-year title, a Monday-to-Sunday grid, and Select and Close buttons.

requirements.statement: The arrival date must fall between 7 days before today and 6 months after today, both ends included, with today taken in Europe/London; the date picker's calendar is bounded by the same window and shows days outside it as excluded.

requirements.statement: The arrival date is typed as day/month/four-digit year, leading zeros optional, must be a real calendar date, is trimmed of surrounding spaces, and is stored as a date with no time.

requirements.deltaNote: A16-015, E10-008 and F-057 show the format, leading-zero tolerance and date-only storage already.

requirements.statement: An arrival date that is not a real date (such as 31/2/2026) is refused with 'Enter a real arrival date', in the summary and inline, keeping what was typed.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express (ruling), so the real service keeps this check.
requirements.deltaNote: F-019 and A16-029 show the message already.

requirements.statement: A typed arrival date outside the window is refused with 'Arrival date at port of entry must be between <earliest> and <latest>', naming the window's ends in d/m/yyyy.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express (ruling), so the real service keeps this check.
requirements.deltaNote: F-020, A16-034 and E10-030 show the message already.

requirements.statement: A saved arrival date that has since fallen outside the window is flagged when the page is reopened, with 'The saved arrival date is no longer a date you can choose. Enter a new arrival date.'

requirements.deltaNote: F-021 and F-056 show the stale-date flag already.

requirements.statement: When arrival details has any error, nothing on the page is saved and the page re-renders with every entry shown back, the refused one included.

requirements.statement: The open calendar sits in the flow of the page and pushes the port question down, and its toggle is a GOV.UK-blue button with a white icon, darkening on hover and keeping the GOV.UK focus style.

requirements.deltaNote: A16-023 to A16-026 show the in-flow calendar and toggle styling already.

requirements.statement: Without JavaScript the arrival date stays an editable text input with the same label and hint, and an in-window date typed there saves.

requirements.deltaNote: F-018 and A16-039 show the no-JavaScript date entry already.

requirements.statement: While a template is being created, arrival details does not show the arrival date question and saves no arrival date, and the section counts as complete without one.

requirements.deltaNote: Today the page always collects the arrival date (F-007).

requirements.statement: The port of entry type-ahead lists every port when clicked, filters as the user types on any part of the port name or the code, case-insensitively, and searches a list rendered into the page with no lookup call.

requirements.statement: The port options come from the reference-data service's GET /ports-of-entry, which reads MDM's border control post points-of-entry list unfiltered and returns each port's code and name.

requirements.deltaNote: F-028 and R-028 show the frontend already reads ports from the reference-data service.

requirements.statement: When MDM answers the ports call with no body or no result list, the reference-data service returns an empty list rather than an error.

requirements.deltaNote: R-035 shows the empty-list fallback already.

requirements.statement: The port of entry list offers Design Release 2.1's ports of entry: the UK and Crown Dependency airports with their IATA codes and the UK seaports with their UN/LOCODEs, without the duplicate records today's list carries (Pembroke Port under GB PED and GB PEM, Port of Sheerness under GBSHS and GB SHS).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 is the target list, but list content is master reference data that MDM supplies, so it waits for the MDM integration (DR1 ruling).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list holds 78 GB ports and airports from reference data, with Pembroke Port and Port of Sheerness each listed twice (A16-043, A16-044, E4-074, E4-075). Design Release 2.1 also has no rail terminal entry (T8-019).
requirements.blockedBy: The MDM integration of master reference data (Rhys's ruling of 2026-09-07) must supply the port list, or a fresh ruling must release the list content for editing before then.

requirements.statement: Port names are spelt correctly: 'Teesport' not 'Teestort', 'Tilbury' not 'TILBURY', and 'Portsmouth Port' with a single space, so typing 'Teesport' finds the port.
requirements.why: Today a misspelt name makes Teesport unfindable; the fix belongs in the MDM source as a data-quality report, not in a fixture MDM replaces (DR1 ruling).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list shows 'Teestort (GB TEE)', 'TILBURY (GB TIL)' and 'Portsmouth  Port (GB PME)' (A16-044, E4-076).
requirements.blockedBy: MDM must correct the three port names, raised with them as a data-quality report, or the MDM integration (Rhys's ruling of 2026-09-07) must land; codes do not change.

requirements.statement: The port list is ordered as Design Release 2.1 orders it: airports first, then seaports in alphabetical order of name, ignoring letter case.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's order puts the busiest entry points first; ordering by port type needs an attribute the list does not carry today, so it waits for MDM.
requirements.deltaNote: Today reference data sorts by name case-sensitively, so 'TILBURY' and 'HES Humber Bulk Terminal' sort before lower-case names (R-030, A16-043-m1).
requirements.blockedBy: The MDM integration (Rhys's ruling of 2026-09-07) must supply each port's type (airport or seaport) before the list can be ordered by it.

requirements.statement: A submitted port not in the list is refused with 'Select a valid option', and the search box is cleared while the other answers are kept.

requirements.deltaNote: F-033 and A16-054 show the refusal already.

requirements.statement: A saved port that is no longer offered is flagged when the page is reopened, with 'The saved port of entry is no longer available. Select a port from the list.', and the field opens empty.

requirements.deltaNote: F-034 shows the stale-port flag already.

requirements.deltaNote: F-032 and A16-053 show the native-select fallback already; Design Release 2.1's port search needs JavaScript.

requirements.statement: Arrival details and transit countries each end with 'Save and continue', a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link.

requirements.statement: When arrival details was opened from the notification review, Save and continue saves and returns to the review.

requirements.statement: 'Save and return to overview' on arrival details and transit countries saves the page and goes to the overview without requiring a means of transport, while the field checks that stay (conflict C1) still apply.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a user leave a part-finished page without being stopped by the required means of transport.

requirements.statement: Saved arrival answers are shown again when the user returns: the date, the chosen port, the means of transport, the transport identification and the document reference.

requirements.statement: The overview's 'Arrival details' task shows Complete only when the arrival date is a real date in the window, the port is on the list, a means of transport is chosen, and transport identification and transport document reference are filled in; otherwise it shows To do.

requirements.statement: A saved arrival date that later falls more than 7 days into the past turns the 'Arrival details' task back to To do.

requirements.statement: When a save fails, arrival details and transit countries re-render with the user's entries and the shared recoverable-error message.

requirements.statement: Each form on both pages posts back without browser validation and carries a CSRF crumb and a concurrency token that rises with each saved change.

requirements.deltaNote: A16-010, A16-011 and E10-073 show the crumb and concurrency token already.

requirements.statement: Arrival details (with the calendar open) and transit countries (empty, with a country added, and in an error state) have no serious or critical axe violations against WCAG 2.2 AA.

conflicts.about: Field validation on arrival details and transit countries: Design Release 2.1 validates softly (only means of transport raises an error), while the real service refuses bad dates, unknown ports and codes, over-long text, repeated or unknown countries and more than 12 countries.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, validation among them, overrides the prototype default.
No error is shown for a missing, badly formed or out-of-range arrival date; it only affects completeness.
No error is shown for a missing or unrecognised port of entry.
Transport identification has no format or length check.
Transport document reference has no format or length check.
The server does not check that a transit country is on the list or not repeated.
When the means of transport error shows, everything else entered is still saved.
An arrival date that is not a real date is refused with 'Enter a real arrival date'.
A port not in the list is refused with 'Select a valid option'.
Transport identification over 58 characters is refused.
Adding a country already in the list is refused by name.
At most 12 transit countries can be added.
When the arrival date is out of window nothing on the page is saved.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first and names validation as a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so the real service keeps every server-side field check and its message: the real-date and window checks on the arrival date, the stale-date and stale-port flags, the in-list checks on port and means of transport, the 58-character limits, and the transit checks (nothing chosen, not on the list, already added, the 12-country cap, stale saved countries). A page with any error saves nothing and shows the entries back. Where Design Release 2.1 does validate (means of transport required on Save and continue) it is adopted. The prototype's soft-validation claims are set aside.

conflicts.about: Design Release 2.1 builds the port and transit-country searches as JavaScript-only components and leaves out accessibility features the real service has: no way to add or remove a transit country without JavaScript, a Remove link with no country name for screen readers, and no 'Error: ' prefix on the page title in an error state.

positions.says: Transit country Remove links have href '#' and work only with JavaScript; no non-JavaScript way to add or remove a country is shown.
Every Remove link reads only 'Remove', with no visually hidden country name.
The page title gains no 'Error: ' prefix when arrival details shows a validation error.
Without JavaScript the country search is a native select that still adds a country, reads the list back and saves.
Each Remove control's accessible name is 'Remove <country>'.
When the arrival page shows validation errors, the page title is prefixed with 'Error: '.

conflicts.outcome: Neither the prototype default nor a DR1 judgement settles it: the ruling does not say whether a feature the real service has that Design Release 2.1 omits is a difference to remove (ruling gap RU-022), and accessibility and working without JavaScript are not among the constraints it names. Raised with a default that splits by environment.
conflicts.question: Where Design Release 2.1's port and transit-country searches need JavaScript and omit the 'Error: ' title prefix and the country name on Remove, should the real service keep its no-JavaScript fallback and those accessibility features?
conflicts.default: With JavaScript, follow Design Release 2.1: picking a transit country adds it straight away with no Add country button, and Remove takes it off without a page load. Without JavaScript, keep today's native selects, the Add country button and the Remove buttons that submit the form. On every page keep the 'Error: ' title prefix and the visually hidden country name on each Remove.

conflicts.about: What the pages submit and store: Design Release 2.1 posts display text (the port as 'name - code', transit countries as a JSON list of names, means of transport as 'Air'), while the real service submits and stores reference codes.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, persistence and cross-service behaviour among them, overrides the prototype default.
The port of entry is posted as the display string 'name - code', not a separate code.
The arrival form posts the means of transport as 'Air' and the port as its display string.
Transit countries are submitted as a JSON list in one hidden field.
Means of transport values are normalised to and stored as Air, Rail, Road and Sea.
Chosen transit countries are held in a hidden field as a JSON array of names.
The transit form posts transitCountries as a URL-encoded JSON array.
Transit countries are submitted as one hidden JSON array of country names.
Transit countries are submitted as one hidden JSON list built client-side.
Each port option submits the port code.
The transited countries answer is saved as a list of country codes.
Each port carries MDM's port code.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the stored answer is read by the backend and other services, a persistence and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express. The real service keeps submitting and storing the port code, the means-of-transport code (AIRPLANE, RAILWAY, ROAD_VEHICLE, VESSEL) and transit country codes. What the user sees still follows Design Release 2.1 (labels, option text), so only the submitted and stored form is set aside.

conflicts.about: The content of the port of entry and transit country lists: Design Release 2.1 offers 205 airports and seaports and 41 countries (EU, outermost regions, Crown Dependencies), while today's lists come from reference data (78 ports, 31 countries) and the DR1 ruling defers list content to MDM.

positions.says: A parity finding whose fix is the content of a master reference-data list is deferred rather than built, because MDM replaces it.
The country-list and port-list increments are blocked on MDM grounds and need a fresh ruling.
The port of entry list holds 205 entries: 28 airports then 177 seaports.
The transit country list offers 41 options: EU states, outermost regions and Crown Dependencies.
Ports are read from MDM's border control post points-of-entry list.
The transit country list is the countries service's origin-country list.

conflicts.outcome: The DR1 judgement on the same difference (Rhys, 2026-09-07) ranks above the prototype: list content is master reference data that MDM supplies after the DR1 parity build, so editing the frontend's lists now is work MDM replaces. Design Release 2.1's list content is adopted as the target but blocked on the MDM integration; until then the pages keep today's reference-data lists. Nothing is overruled: the prototype's lists stay the target, only deferred.

conflicts.about: Which arrival date Design Release 2.1 collects: its question page asks for the arrival date at the port of entry, but its review page labels the same answer 'Arrival date at destination'.

positions.says: The arrival details page labels the field 'Arrival date at port of entry'.
The review labels the arrival date 'Arrival date at destination'.
DR1 contradicted itself the same way between its question page and its review page and dashboard cards.
Whether the date is arrival at the port of entry or at the destination is undecided, and nothing changes until it is ruled.
The real frontend labels the question, the check-answers row and the validation message 'Arrival date at port of entry'.

conflicts.outcome: The design contradicts itself across two of its own pages, as DR1 did, and the DR1 finding (inc-145) was deferred without a judgement, so neither precedence nor a ruling settles it. A port of entry and a place of destination are different places in this service, so only one label can be right.
conflicts.question: Is the arrival date the expected arrival at the port of entry or at the place of destination?
conflicts.default: The port of entry: keep 'Arrival date at port of entry' on the question page, the review row and the out-of-window error message, matching the stored field (arrivalDateAtPort) and the field's hint.

conflicts.about: The worked example in the arrival date hint: Design Release 2.1 uses a fixed '27/3/2026', while the real service shows today's date so the example is always a date the window accepts.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, validation among them, overrides the prototype default.
The hint is 'The expected date of arrival at the port of entry. For example, 27/3/2026'.
The rendered hint ends 'For example, 27/3/2026'.
The spec asserts the hint with the fixed example 27/3/2026.
The example is today's date in Europe/London.
The worked example is always a date the page accepts.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first. The real service keeps its arrival-date window (conflict on validation), and a fixed 27/3/2026 already falls outside that window, so a user who copied the example would be refused. The validation the prototype cannot express overrides its fixed example: the hint keeps its Design Release 2.1 wording with today's date as the example.
